Time: 5 minutes
Outcome: Measure Profit, Loss & Break-Even.
Difficulty: Intermediate
THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: Economic profit or loss equals the gap between price and average total cost multiplied by output. Profit, Loss & Break-Even measures per-unit and total economic profit or loss and interpret break-even and zero economic profit. The firm combines its revenue from price and quantity with all economic costs to measure profit. Profit/loss measurement and the short-run shutdown decision use different comparisons. Separate output, operating status, profit or loss, and long-run entry or exit pressure.

WATCH OUT

runs.text: Do not confuse loss with shutdown. Profit/loss measurement and the short-run shutdown decision use different comparisons. Economic cost includes implicit opportunity costs, including the normal return needed to keep owner resources in the firm.

transcript.text: The market sets a price of 15 dollars . The representative firm produces 50 units where P equals M R equals M C , but its ATC is 18 dollars . Loss per unit is 18 dollars minus 15 dollars equals 3 dollars , so total loss is 3 dollars times 50 equals 150 dollars . The firm may still operate because price exceeds AVC.

WORKED EXAMPLE: PROFIT, LOSS, OR BREAK-EVEN?

The market sets a price of $15. The representative firm produces 50 units where P = MR = MC, but its ATC is $18. Loss per unit is $18 - $15 = $3, so total loss is $3 x 50 = $150. The firm may still operate because price exceeds AVC.
